misconceptions.description: Assuming that if a policy does not mention AI then any AI use is permitted
misconceptions.trigger: teacher justifies a practice by saying the policy says nothing against it
misconceptions.feedback: Silence is not permission. When the written policy is silent, apply the governing principles (FERPA, district data rules) and seek clarification rather than assuming approval.

misconceptions.description: Applying policy language literally without interpreting its intent for the situation at hand
misconceptions.trigger: teacher follows the letter of a rule in a way that defeats its purpose
misconceptions.feedback: Read for the policy's purpose, not only its words. Interpret ambiguous language toward the goal it protects, such as student privacy or equitable access.

misconceptions.description: Believing one school AI policy answers every question without checking overlapping rules
misconceptions.trigger: teacher consults only the AI-use memo and ignores privacy, special-education, or consent rules
misconceptions.feedback: AI decisions sit at the intersection of several policies. Check the AI memo against FERPA, IEP/504 requirements, consent rules, and acceptable-use terms together.

misconceptions.description: Treating a policy as fixed and not flagging gaps or harms back to decision-makers
misconceptions.trigger: teacher applies an outdated or harmful policy without documenting the problem
misconceptions.feedback: Policies evolve. When a rule produces an inequitable or unsafe result, document the case and route it to the policy owner so the rule can be revised.
